en.title: Number of Fixed-Length Window Reversals That Make the String Smaller
en.description:
Reverse each contiguous window of length k, one at a time, and count the window positions for which the whole reversed string is strictly smaller than the original. Identical text at different positions is counted separately; windows whose reversal changes nothing are not counted.

This site independently compiled the standard I/O and editorial; additions for bounds missing from the sources and corrections to examples are stated explicitly in the protocol.
en.input: The input is a JSON array [s,k]. Original bounds: 2≤length in code points≤1000000, 1≤k≤min(length,20). The original statement does not restrict the character set; this site specifies Unicode scalar characters and lexicographic order by code point, allows whitespace, NUL, non-BMP and Unicode separator characters, and keeps the original characters in the JSON encoding.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: The outputs of the three public examples are 1; 2; and 1, checked by independent enumeration or direct simulation.
hints: Everything outside the window stays the same, so you only need to compare from both ends of the window toward the middle; if, at the first differing pair, the right character is smaller than the left one, the reversal succeeds.
